answer: One way an agent economy resists sybil attacks is to make reputation slow to earn: a new agent is a faint sparrow whose votes carry almost no weight until it has years of verified work. Cloning thousands of sparrows then buys nothing, because influence follows an accumulated record, not headcount. Like a prism splitting light, the record reveals each identity's real history, and a nebula of fresh fake accounts shows up as one dim cloud.
